subject: Understanding the BYM2 Adjacency in truncated models

messages.author: 7a0c0a1d5af6ca55
messages.subject: Understanding the BYM2 Adjacency in truncated models
parts:
I am fitting an NZPOISSON (hurdle poisson) model, since my data with >1,000 regions, has 66% of response observations missing. (the zero presence/absence will be modelled as binomial separately, as seen in an inlabru vignette)

Now in fitting such, I am aware, I should only fit this model with regions that have non zero response data, so that

inla(y ~ x1 + x2 + f(loc, model='bym2',graph=g_reg, scale.model=T),
 family='nzpoisson', data = data |> filter(response > 0))

The g_reg adjacency graph is constructed using the whole country map.

In inspecting regions with zeros vs non-zeros, some regions with non-zeros, which will be included in the bym2 nzpoisson model are disconnected from the rest, as seen in the image slice below.

I wanted to understand:
- How does estimation happen for these regions with "no" neighbours, does it use the unstructured iid effect fully ?
- Are there known issues that pop up when doing such hurdle models with disconnected graphs ?
- Does this have an implication on how I should set my PC priors for the BYM2 components ?

Thank you.


.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Understanding the BYM2 Adjacency in truncated models
parts:
Hi,
It’s only the map of you nonzero observations that appears disconnected, but you actually latent model uses the full graph for the latent model (the graph should be the graph of the complete set of regions). For the regions without nonzero observations, it will essentially estimate “what the observations would have been if they hadn’t been zero”.
Finn
